source_text: Καί τις ὀνόματι Ναόδωρος — ὁ καὶ Ἀπελλῆς — πατὴρ πόλεως, καὶ ἄλλος τις, νεωκόρος, ἐμμανόμενος καὶ αὐτὸς τῇ ἀσεβείᾳ τῶν εἰδώλων, ἠξίωσαν τὸν ἡγεμόνα δοθῆναι αὐτοῖς βοήθειαν, ὥστε ζητῆσαι ἐν οἷς ὑπώπτευον τόποις. Καί τις βοηθὸς ὀνόματι Ὠριγένης, ἐπιβὰς καὶ αὐτὸς σὺν τῷ προειρημένῳ Ναοδώρῳ μετὰ καὶ εἰρηναρχικῆς τάξεως καὶ ἑτέρων τινῶν, ηὗρον τὸν μακάριον Κόνωνα ἐν τόπῳ τινὶ λεγομένῳ Καρμενᾷ, βασιλικὸν ἐπαρδεύοντα κῆπον. Καὶ ἐγγίσαντες τῷ τρισμακαρίῳ μάρτυρι ἠσπάζοντο αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Χαῖρε, Κόνων. Καὶ ὁ τοῦ Χριστοῦ δοῦλος, ἡ ἀκέραιος ψυχή, ὁ ἄκακος τῇ διανοίᾳ, λέγει πρὸς αὐτούς· Χαίρετε καὶ ὑμεῖς, τέκνα. Ὁ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ὠριγένης· Παπία, καλεῖ σε ὁ ἡγεμών. Ὁ ἅγιος Κόνων λέγει· Καὶ ἐμοῦ ὁ ἡγεμὼν τί χρείαν ἔχει, ξένου ἀνθρώπου καὶ μάλιστα Χριστιανοῦ; Ἐὰν ζητῇ τοὺς ὁμοίους ἑαυτοῦ, ζητείτω, καὶ οὐχὶ ἄνθρωπον γεωπόνον, μοχθοῦντα τὸ καθ᾽ ἡμέραν. Καὶ ἐπαπορηθεὶς ὁ παράνομος Ναόδωρος ἐπὶ τῇ ἀντιλογίᾳ τοῦ ἁγίου Κόνωνος, κελεύει δεθῆναι αὐτὸν τῷ ἵππῳ αὐτοῦ καὶ οὕτως ἕλκεσθαι. Καὶ ὁ ἅγιος μάρτυς οὐδὲν ἀντεῖπεν τοῖς ἐφέλκουσιν αὐτόν, ἀλλὰ πράως καὶ ἐπιεικῶς ἐπηκολούθει τοῖς παρανόμοις.
pass_a_gloss: And one man by name Naodoros, the one also called Apelles, a father of a city, and another man, a temple-warden, himself also raving in the impiety of the idols, thought it fit to ask the governor for help to be given to them so that they might search in the places they suspected; and a helper by name Origenes, having also mounted with the aforementioned Naodoros with both a peace-keeping detachment and some others, found the blessed Conon in a certain place called Karmena watering an imperial garden; and having come near to the thrice-blessed martyr they greeted him saying Hail, Conon; and the servant of Christ, the undivided soul, the guileless in mind, says to them Hail also to you, children; Origenes says to him Old man, the governor calls you; Saint Conon says What need does the governor have of me, a stranger-man and especially a Christian, if he seeks those like himself let him seek, and not a farming man laboring day by day; and the lawless Naodoros, at a loss at the answer-back of Saint Conon, orders him to be bound to his horse and so to be dragged; and the holy martyr said nothing back to those dragging him, but gently and mildly followed after the lawless men.
pass_b_english: A man named Naodoros, also called Apelles, a father of the city, and another man, a temple-warden himself maddened by devotion to the idols, asked the governor to grant them assistance so they could search the places they suspected. A helper named Origenes then set out with the aforementioned Naodoros, together with a peace-keeping detachment and some others, and they found the blessed Conon at a place called Karmena, where he was watering the imperial garden. Coming up to the thrice-blessed martyr, they greeted him and said, Hail, Conon.

And the servant of Christ, the undivided soul, the guileless in mind, said to them, Hail to you also, children. Origenes said to him, Old fellow, the governor summons you. Saint Conon said, What need does the governor have of me, a stranger and above all a Christian. If he seeks men like himself, let him seek them, and not a field-working man who toils day by day. Then the lawless Naodoros, baffled by Saint Conon's defiant answer, ordered him to be tied to his horse and dragged along in that way. The holy martyr made no reply to those dragging him, but meekly and patiently followed behind the lawless men.

choices.why: nominative in apposition to Naodoros marking a civic dignity, not literal parenthood; preserves the honorific sense

choices.term: νεωκόρος, ἐμμανόμενος τῇ ἀσεβείᾳ τῶν εἰδώλων
choices.english: temple-warden, himself maddened by devotion to the idols
choices.why: dative gives the cause of the frenzy and genitive limits the impiety to idol worship; context is active pagan cult service
vocative address from Origenes is condescending and familiar, not yet a church office; avoids anachronistic clerical title

choices.term: ἄνθρωπον γεωπόνον, μοχθοῦντα τὸ καθ᾽ ἡμέραν
choices.english: a field-working man who toils day by day
choices.why: accusative in contrast to τοὺς ὁμοίους ἑαυτοῦ; participial phrase stresses daily labor as reason he is beneath the governor's notice
